_meta.og_title: Topolograph - OSPF, OSPFv3 and IS-IS topology visualization
_meta.og_description: Analyze OSPF and IS-IS topology from LSDB snapshots or live watcher streams. Run what-if failure scenarios, inspect backup paths, monitor IGP changes, and automate network topology checks through API, Python SDK, MCP Server and AI agents.

lp_eyebrow: Topolograph · routing analysis for network operations
lp_h1: Your network, as its protocols see it
lp_lead: Topolograph builds a model of the network from what its routing protocols report. Each new source adds its own independent layer to that model. Everything else is computed on it: primary and backup paths, links with no backup, search over network elements (prefixes, MAC addresses and more), and link or node failures simulated before maintenance starts. Analysis works from a single LSDB snapshot; a collector adds the stream of changes, and an AI agent answers questions from the same data.
lp_tech: OSPF · OSPFv3 · IS-IS · BGP / EVPN · {count} vendors
lp_iso_aria: Four layers: routers, the Topolograph model, watcher events, agent answers
lp_iso_l3_sub: answers from the same data · MCP
lp_q0_d: Comparing the graph at different moments shows when the prefix left the network.
lp_q1_q: Can a link or a device be taken out of service?
lp_q1_d: Simulating the failure on the graph shows where the traffic goes and which segments are left without a backup, before the work starts.
lp_q2_q: Where will a new MPLS TE LSP with the required bandwidth go?
lp_q2_d: CSPF over the TE attributes from the LSDB shows the LSP path for the requested bandwidth and how it behaves when a link fails.
lp_q3_d: The collector event history and the graph at the time of the incident show what changed and in which order.
lp_q4_q: Where is the virtual machine with this MAC address now?
lp_q4_d: An EVPN MAC lookup shows which VTEP or PE advertises it and which path the traffic takes to it.
lp_q5_q: The interface is up, so why is the adjacency not Full?
lp_q5_d: The protocol shows that there is no adjacency, and Agent 2.0 checks the cause, for example MTU, with read-only commands from an approved runbook.
lp_story_heading: How Topolograph learns your network and works with it
lp_beat_0_h: An LSDB snapshot becomes a network model
lp_beat_0_ask: What does a single snapshot give you?
lp_beat_0_p: The output of {command} from one router becomes a static snapshot of the network: 13 routers, 26 links. You work with it offline, without access to the routers: path calculation, search over network elements, maintenance planning. The diagram shows the pe15 → pe30 path: cost 41, four equal-cost paths.
lp_beat_1_h: A link failure on the model
lp_beat_1_ask: Can a link or a device be taken out of service?
lp_beat_1_p: The core10 ↔ core30 link is switched off on the model: SPF is recalculated, traffic moves to core11 ↔ core31, the cost goes from 41 to 50, and there are still four paths. The real network is not touched.
lp_beat_2_h: The collector as a network sensor
lp_beat_2_ask: What is changing in the network right now?
lp_beat_2_p: The Topolograph collector (watcher) receives routing protocol updates and passes on events about topology changes. It joins the network in one of three ways: a plain IGP adjacency, an IGP adjacency over GRE, or BGP-LS; in the demo it is a GRE adjacency with rr1. When the pe15 ↔ core110 link goes down, both of its ends flood new Router LSAs, the update reaches the collector, and a timestamped event arrives in Topolograph. Of the four pe15 → pe30 paths, two remain.
lp_beat_3_ask: What did the network look like at the time of the incident?
lp_beat_3_p: The timeline replays the collector events: the pe14 → core110 metric, the pe15 ↔ core110 link going down and coming back, a new network on core31, a TE metric. The cursor then moves between T+3 s and T+5 s: four paths before the failure, two after it. The T0 snapshot and any later state can be compared.
lp_beat_4_h: The AI agent answers from the same data
lp_beat_4_ask: What happened in the network in the last 15 minutes?
lp_beat_4_p: The engineer asks the question. The agent calls the Topolograph MCP server tools for events and failure calculation, and answers with a reference to the data. Agent 2.0 already diagnoses incidents with a runbook agreed in advance: on an engineer's request, or automatically when an event opens a ticket. Read-only access, authorization and the explicit runbook steps make the diagnosis safe and several times faster.

lp_mon_heading: Existing monitoring and Topolograph: complementing and extending network visibility
lp_mon_sub: Zabbix, Prometheus and Cacti watch devices and interfaces. Topolograph shows how the network routes traffic and works alongside them.

lp_dep_self_p: Topolograph and the routing protocol collectors run in your infrastructure; the routing data and the history of network states stay under your control.
lp_dep_saas_h: Hosted (SaaS) with an on-site collector sensor
lp_dep_saas_p: A physical collector sensor on your site receives the routing data locally and passes the agreed data to the hosted Topolograph over a protected channel.
lp_ed_sub: Community: offline analysis of snapshots, free and in your own infrastructure. Enterprise: continuous protocol monitoring and teamwork.
lp_ed_note_reupload: Re-uploading the LSDB through the API is also available in Community, but these are snapshots on demand, not a stream of watcher events.
